articles.title: PhotoWalk AI: A Photography Challenge That Gets You Outside
articles.excerpt: PhotoWalk AI — Turning Screen Time Into Real-World Exploration This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass I built PhotoWalk AI, a web application that enco…
articles.body: PhotoWalk AI — Turning Screen Time Into Real-World Exploration This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built I built PhotoWalk AI, a web application that encourages people to go outside and turn a normal walk into a photography challenge. The idea came from something pretty simple: we spend a lot of time looking at photos on our phones, but not enough time actually going outside and creating our own experiences. PhotoWalk AI gives users a reason to explore their surroundings. Users can create a PhotoWalk and get creative photography missions such as finding interesting shadows, reflections, colors, or other things around them. They then go outside, complete the mission, and upload their best photographs.

articles.title: How to Write a Spec an AI App Builder Can Actually Ship
articles.excerpt: How to Write a Spec an AI App Builder Can Actually Ship AI app builders can now produce a working full-stack app from a description. The catch is the description. "Build me a CRM" gets you a pretty de…
articles.body: How to Write a Spec an AI App Builder Can Actually Ship AI app builders can now produce a working full-stack app from a description. The catch is the description. "Build me a CRM" gets you a pretty demo with fake data. A short, structured spec gets you something close to a real product. Here's the spec format that consistently produces usable Next.js apps on the first or second try. Why vague prompts fail An AI builder has to make hundreds of decisions: data model, auth, routes, validation, empty states. Every decision you leave out, it guesses. Guesses compound. By the time you notice the data model is wrong, three screens are built on top of it. A spec doesn't need to be long. It needs to answer the questions the builder would otherwise guess. The one-page spec 1.

articles.body: Cada vez que tocás "Continuar con Google" en una app nueva y nunca escribís una contraseña, estás usando OAuth 2.0. El protocolo se formalizó en el RFC 6749 en octubre de 2012 y hoy sostiene casi todo inicio de sesión delegado de la web. Entenderlo a fondo evita dos errores frecuentes entre desarrolladores: tratarlo como un sistema de login y copiar ejemplos de flujos ya deprecados. Este artículo explica sus roles, sus flujos vigentes y los errores que más rompen implementaciones reales.

articles.title: While your build runs, walk
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass. A GitHub Actions run already knows how long it is. You start it, and then you sit there, watching a bar that ha…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . What I Built A GitHub Actions run already knows how long it is. You start it, and then you sit there, watching a bar that has already done the counting. Build Break takes that length and puts it on the phone. You paste a public repository, press start, and the screen becomes a clock that stays awake. You leave. If the street is worth keeping, you take one photo. When the run finishes, or when you decide you are done, a short journal entry is waiting. The first screen says the whole thing in one breath. While your build runs, walk. Snap what you see. An open model writes the entry when you get back. The screen is a glance. The walk is the rest of it.

articles.title: One Coercion Table Moves Only After Twelve Export Rows Hold
articles.excerpt: One Coercion Table Moves Only After Twelve Export Rows Hold One coercion table moves only after twelve export rows hold. A messy mapper stays untouched until those frozen rows match. The smallest safe…
articles.body: One Coercion Table Moves Only After Twelve Export Rows Hold One coercion table moves only after twelve export rows hold. A messy mapper stays untouched until those frozen rows match. The smallest safe change is one pure coercion table. The problem in one pass Export helpers grow by one silent exception at a time. A null note becomes an empty string in one branch. A numeric string becomes an integer minor unit in another. Callers then depend on both accidents without a written contract. A broad rewrite looks faster than a pinned fixture run. It also hides which accident a downstream report still needs. Pin the current map before you touch the helper body. Move one coercion table only after those rows stay green. Treat any extra cleanup as a separate, later change.

articles.title: NASA dumped over 800GB of Artemis II data online
articles.excerpt: A crew annotated image showing where the Artemis II team observed impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. | Image: NASA If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission,…
articles.body: A crew annotated image showing where the Artemis II team observed impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. | Image: NASA If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission , you're wrong. This week NASA posted over 800GB worth of science data, images, and videos on the Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science site. The archive includes over 11,000 photos and videos, over 8.5 hours of audio, and crew-annotated images, such as the one marking where they saw impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. Together, they offer an unprecedented view inside a historic space mission. One of the more exciting reveals was footage of the Artemis II team telling the ground team back in Houston about its observation of impact flashes.

articles.body: There are over 230 million copies of Grand Theft Auto 5 in the world. As the second-highest selling game of all time, it has been played for billions of hours by players across the globe, making it one of the most significant pastimes in the entire world. That’s an impressive achievement for what in 2013 was simply the highly-anticipated next entry in Rockstar’s beloved (and notorious) open-world crime series. But GTA 5 proved to be much, much more than a typical sequel. It has become home to a huge, expressive, and loyal community, one which has made a digital hobby of everything from warring alien clans to producing slick vehicle stunt movies. This is the story of how a video game became much more than a crime simulator.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 10… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Lunar Farside Explanation: Tidally locked in synchronous rotation , the Moon always presents its familiar nearside to denizens of planet Earth . From lunar orbit, the Moon’s farside can become familiar, though. In fact this sharp picture , a mosaic from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter’s wide angle camera, is centered on the lunar farside.

articles.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
articles.excerpt: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that…
articles.body: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested an executive at a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity. The New York Times reported today that the FBI has arrested a Canadian man in Pennsylvania on suspicion of assisting ShinyHunters. The Times story did not identify the man, nor did a statement on Twitter/X about the arrest from FBI Director Kash Patel .

articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars.
